R phaseY phaseB phase L1 ringL2 ringL3 ring

1. The diagram, as built

  • Coil groups and polarity: R = +1 +6 −7 −12, Y = −4 +5 +10 −11, B = +2 −3 −8 +9 (12 slots, 10 poles)
  • Delta: L1 = R + B′, L2 = R′ + Y, L3 = Y′ + B — one copper ring per line terminal
  • Each phase: 2 parallel paths × 2 coils in series; coil 104 A, phase 208 A, line 360 A
  • All 12 coils are the same part; a coil's polarity is set only by which lead is fed. “+” = current enters at S (start), “−” = enters at F (finish).

2. Every parallel path traced through the busbar

Read left to right: line ring → coil lead → coil (polarity) → series link → coil (polarity) → coil lead → line ring. Both paths of a phase must give the same EMF (otherwise they short each other), and the three phases must close the delta (sum = 0).

Delta EMF sum: 1.6e-15 (closed and balanced). Each path EMF 1.932 = two coils adding (a reversed coil would give 0.518).

3. Busbar layout

Four copper levels in the carrier, bottom to top: series links, L2, L3, L1. Every ring is 10 × 3 mm (30 mm²). Each coil lead has its own tab that stands up beside the lead to the weld plane (z 66.0); lead and tab end flush and are welded there. Terminals L1/L2/L3: vertical blades with Ø6.6 holes.

Busbar, carrier hidden: every conductor a separate part

Busbar top view

One tooth: start lead (inner layer) steps out once then rises; finish lead rises straight from the slot

Full stator
